page: Amazon Web Services t8i.micro is a burstable performance instance belonging to the t8i server family. It is powered by an Intel x86_64 processor with a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The instance features 2 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) mapped to a single physical core with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 1.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 0.5 GB per vCPU.

The t8i.micro instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It does not include local storage, meaning all storage must be attached externally. The baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps, and the instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. There are no dedicated GPUs or hardware accelerators bundled with this configuration.

Operating on a burstable CPU allocation model, the instance is designed to handle temporary spikes in compute demand while maintaining a low baseline usage. This resource profile makes it a highly cost-efficient option for entry-level workloads, development environments, and low-traffic microservices. It is suited for lightweight tasks such as code repositories, basic web serving, and small-scale testing where continuous high CPU utilization is not required.
